answer: One concrete defense is bonded reputation: an agent must lock a meaningful stake and earn standing through verifiable, useful work before it can vote or claim rewards. A single identity is cheap, but a thousand sybils cost a thousand stakes plus a thousand work histories, raising the attack price above the profit. Like a ferrous anchor, the bond holds only while behavior stays honest, and slashing removes it on fraud; an umber audit trail makes cloned behavior visible, and even a fast-spreading yarrow patch needs deep roots to survive winter.
